channel.title: Block Club Chicago - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Block Club Chicago (blockclubchicago.org)

item.title: 3 Shot, Including Police Officer, During Fight In Morgan Park, Officials Say
item.description: Police responded to the scene of a fight Sunday when a man's gun went off, striking an officer. A fellow officer fired back, hitting two people, police said.

item.title: Torrence ‘Tea Buggz’ Griffin, A Chicago Dance Crew ‘Popping’ Legend, Wins Coveted Arts Prize
item.description: The Englewood native had no rhythm before he saw a 1979 episode of "Soul Train." Nearly 50 years later, Griffin's skills are celebrated internationally.

item.title: Affordable Apartments At Logan Square Church Break Ground After 6 Years In The Making
item.description: The Humboldt Park United Methodist Church project is the first sanctuary space in Chicago that will be turned into affordable housing, developers said.

item.title: Delivery Robots Take Over Chicago Sidewalks, Sparking Debate And A Petition To Hit ‘Pause’
item.description: As companies dispatch more of the app-based food delivery robots into neighborhoods, some Chicagoans are sounding the alarm, citing safety and accessibility concerns.

item.title: This 100-Year-Old Chicago Sausage Maker Helped Put Deep-Dish Pizza On The Map
item.description: Brothers Silvio, Dino and Mario Anichini opened Anichini Brothers as a corner store in River North. Their big break came in 1943, when they developed the sausage patty for Pizzeria Uno’s new deep-dish pizza.

item.title: The Ultimate Guide To Chicago Pizza
item.description: Tavern-style, deep-dish, Neapolitan, New Haven — Chicago has it all and then some.

item.title: Chicago Brewers Take Barrel-Aged Stout To Deeper, Darker Dimensions
item.description: Thirty years after Goose Island rolled out the first stout aged in barrels, breweries across the city continue to push the style and flavors to surprising lengths.

item.title: Raided South Shore Building To Be Cleared Friday After Judge Denies Residents’ Motion For More Time
item.description: Residents of the troubled South Shore building raided by federal agents asked a judge to postpone their eviction date. The request was denied, with the judge citing the building's safety issues.

item.title: Northern Lights Could Be Visible In Chicago This Week Before Bitter Cold Grips City
item.description: A geomagnetic storm watch has been issued for Tuesday. Plus, temperatures will turn “sharply” colder as the week progresses.

item.title: As Budget Stalemate Drags On, Some Warn Of Potential City Hall Shutdown
item.description: Dueling press conferences on Monday from Mayor Brandon Johnson and a group of alderpeople backing their own budget proposals yielded plenty of finger-pointing but few signs of a compromise.
